title: Anthropic Cuts Rival AI Data Harvesting by 90% to 99%
summary:
The AI developer has banned tens of thousands of accounts after identifying attempts by competitors to siphon intelligence from its Claude models. New technical defenses have reduced the amount of data rivals can extract via distillation—using a powerful model to train a smaller one—by 90% to 99%. Anthropic named Chinese labs Zhipu and Moonshot as attackers and detected one network using over 20,000 fake accounts, including a user it believes was affiliated with China's People's Liberation Army who used the system to analyze CCTV surveillance.

The safeguards have turned away trillions of tokens of paying traffic and meaningful revenue, though the company began charging for certain blocked extraction requests on September 24. While the current classifier has a false-positive rate below 0.1%, some users report that legitimate evaluation runs have been flagged. Anthropic noted its defenses have not yet faced a highly sophisticated or persistent attempt to bypass them, but the results suggest technical defenses may be more effective than the government regulations previously sought to protect intellectual property.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Anthropic, not the government, was in the best position to stop distillation of its own models
selectedTweets.text:
Anthropic says it has reduced the data harvested from Claude in distillation attacks by around 90–99%. I congratulate them on this achievement.

It’s consistent with the point I made a few months ago (All-In Ep. 282): Anthropic, not the government, was in the best position to stop distillation of its own models. Once the horse is out of the barn, there’s limited value in after-the-fact government action.

At the time there was a major push in Washington to restrict open models on IP grounds. The threat looked serious enough that 50 companies — including Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, IBM, Palantir, and Dell — published an open letter in defense of open-weight models. Jensen Huang promoted it in his first-ever X post. Nearly 200 startups sent a similar letter.

I argued that restricting open models risked removing the incentive for closed-model companies to solve the problem themselves — and could reward negligence by stifling competition while they continued collecting revenue from distillation. The administration did not impose those restrictions.

Now we see the result. Anthropic invested in defenses and they worked. Not every technical challenge is a reason to run to Washington for new regulation.

Anthropic says new safeguards have cut the distillation that rival labs can pull out of Claude by 10 to 100 times ("around 90 to 99 percent"). 

Anthropic names Chinese labs Zhipu and Moonshot, and says one network once ran more than 20,000 fake accounts at a time.

It remains to be seen whether GLM and Kimi will continue to release outstanding models when they can barely distill anymore.

selectedTweets.bestBit: removed tens of thousands of accounts, often within two hours of detecting a campaign
selectedTweets.text:
Anthropic says it has cut the Claude reasoning harvested by rival model developers by 90% to 99%.

The target is distillation: collecting a stronger model's responses to train another model. Detailed reasoning transcripts are particularly valuable because they show how Claude reaches its answers.

The new defenses block extraction prompts, restrict moving reasoning between accounts and models, and ban repeat offenders. Anthropic says it has removed tens of thousands of accounts, often within two hours of detecting a campaign.

There are trade-offs for paying users too: some integrations need changes, and blocked extraction requests are now charged. The results are Anthropic's own measurements, and it acknowledges that the defenses haven't yet faced a highly sophisticated, persistent attempt to bypass them.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Industrial distillers will suck the value out their best models for cheap
selectedTweets.text:
We’ve had legit eval runs flagged as suspected distillation and refused. It’s annoying when you’re trying to test a model.

Anthropic is candid here about about how much of a high-stakes cat-and-mouse game this is.

If they can’t make distillation impossible, it’s hard to call training frontier models a defensible business. Industrial distillers will suck the value out their best models for cheap.
